synthesis: The family measure is first compressed by the three indicators into unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic proportions; low-zero symmetry then requires two independent refinements before the universality table applies: remove persistent central zeros measured by the next-order rank statistic, and split the symplectic mass by the ramified root number. Only after those steps does conductor scaling send rank-zero homogeneous pieces to U, Sp, SOeven, or SOodd statistics, so the random-matrix class is obtained by a composed inference rather than by reading a group name.
source_support: Unit u05 defines the Sato–Tate measure, the indicators i1, i2, i3, and the unique U/O/Sp mass equations despite nonunique compact-group decompositions. Unit u06 separately defines rank from the next-order local coefficient, requires persistent central zeros to be removed, and refines symplectic families by epsilon using ramified local factors and Möbius cancellation. Unit u07 then states the conductor-scaled universality table for rank-zero homogeneous families, omits the forced central zero in the epsilon=-1 case, and weights mixed families by the earlier decomposition.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compose three distinct representation changes: project the prime-averaged local measure to type masses via trace moments, correct the central-zero ensemble by rank and root-sign data not contained in that measure, and then apply the homogeneity-to-low-zero reversal table after conductor normalization.
limits: The finite product-measure and general Sato–Tate statements are conjectural at the stated level, the indicator consequences retain the source's asymptotic and RH assumptions, rank identification can depend on Tate-type conjectures, and root-sign proportions may require Chowla-type Möbius cancellation. The low-zero universality step is explicitly deeper, assumes the relevant analytic continuation, and is supported in general only conditionally or for restricted test-function support.
quality_reason: All three units are necessary for the claimed pipeline: u05 alone cannot determine rank or root sign, u06 alone does not select a random-matrix law, and u07 presupposes the rank-zero homogeneous refinement constructed by the earlier stages. The synthesis preserves the distinction between leading local equidistribution, next-order bias, ramified parity, and the deeper zero-statistics conjecture.

synthesis: Harmonic and geometric families reach comparable local and Sato–Tate measures through different averaging engines. In the harmonic route, the identity orbital term produces unramified Plancherel mass and the L-map pushes it to Satake statistics; in the geometric route, parameter counting first descends modulo p to an atomic Frobenius measure, and a lisse sheaf's monodromy turns that measure into a Haar pushforward. The common output is a family measure, but the representations compressed and the error burdens carried by the two routes remain different.
source_support: Unit u12 derives the harmonic local measure by pushing unramified Plancherel measure through r, with the identity conjugacy class as main term and all other orbital integrals controlling the uniform error. Unit u13 uses Macdonald's formula to pass from that measure to the dual-group Sato–Tate group, indicators, and rank zero while retaining root-number and analytic-continuation burdens. Unit u19 shows that good-reduction Satake classes depend only on w modulo p, converting integer-parameter averages to a finite atomic measure off the discriminant. Unit u20 packages those Frobenius classes in a lisse sheaf and uses Deligne–Katz equidistribution to identify the limit as the Haar pushforward from geometric monodromy; it explicitly compares the natural harmonic and geometric family groups.
nonparaphrase_operation: Align the two source-specific chains at their shared measure-level codomain: trace-formula identity term -> Plancherel measure -> L-map pushforward, versus integer parameters -> reduction modulo p -> Frobenius atomic measure -> monodromy Haar pushforward. This exposes exactly which intermediate representation and error estimate each construction uses and forgets.
limits: The harmonic argument is strongest for regular cohomological or discrete-series settings; higher-rank Maass families retain continuous-spectrum and uniform orbital-integral obstacles, and actual cuspidality of lifts is separate from essential cuspidality. The geometric outline suppresses technical hypotheses, removes finitely many primes, and uses purity/monodromy assumptions; number-field low-zero conclusions additionally require modularity and analytic input. The comparison identifies parallel measure-producing mechanisms, not an equivalence of their groups or proof theories.
quality_reason: The relation is unavailable from either route alone and is concrete at every bridge object: identity orbital mass and Plancherel pushforward on one side, finite-field Frobenius atoms and monodromy Haar measure on the other. Units u13 and u20 also justify the common Sato–Tate endpoint while preserving distinct bottlenecks, so the synthesis is more than a thematic comparison.

synthesis: A statistically usable family needs two independent resources: a controlled counting measure on its parameters and a positive-mass mechanism for isolating its spectral conditions. Finite-to-one parametrization, or explicit substitute constraints, makes conductor balls finite and local coefficient averages meaningful; unrestricted Diophantine bases or intersections can destroy those averages. Positive Plancherel volume supplies the trace-formula isolation mechanism, whereas a Plancherel-null condition removes that ordinary counting resource. These tractability conditions delimit where the proposed ensemble statistics can be formed, without deciding whether the individual L-functions are mathematically natural.
source_support: Unit u03 builds harmonic families only from trace-formula-isolable positive-Plancherel sets, keeps parameter spaces as part of family counting, and warns that intersections introduce global Diophantine equations. Unit u04 requires finite conductor counts and an infinite family, obtains finiteness from finite-to-one maps or imposed parameter restrictions, and formulates the vertical average only after that ordering is fixed. Unit u21 makes the intersection warning concrete: general Diophantine parameter sets can encode arbitrary recursive subsets for which even the coefficient averages need not exist. Unit u23 shows the independent spectral obstruction: measure-zero local conditions cannot be effectively isolated by the ordinary trace formula, and even conductor enumeration is difficult.
nonparaphrase_operation: Stress-test the family definition along two orthogonal axes: replace controlled parameter counting by a Diophantine intersection and observe loss of asymptotic averages, then replace a positive-volume spectral constraint by a Plancherel-null one and observe loss of the trace-formula identity-term counting mechanism.
limits: Finite-to-one parametrization is sufficient but not necessary because suitable cones, gauges, or other constraints can restore finite counting. Positive Plancherel volume is a requirement of the source's effective trace-formula construction, not a proof that every null family violates the conjectures; u23 poses their validity as an open question. Natural nonparametric families may still have the predicted statistics when additional counting hypotheses, such as strong Hardy–Littlewood behavior, are available.
quality_reason: The synthesis combines two distinct failure modes that no single parent supplies: u04/u21 govern whether the parameter ensemble and its averages exist, while u03/u23 govern whether local spectral restrictions have a usable main-term mass. The conclusion is therefore a concrete boundary on the source's statistical framework rather than a generic claim that tractability is desirable.
